exercise.name: Bodyweight Overhead Forward Lunge

reference.title: Bodyweight Overhead Forward Lunge (male)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee and ankle; both arms held overhead)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step forward and lower, exhale as you push back to standing; keep the ribs down under the raised arms.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.7 s push back

prescription.tempo: Controlled step, 1-2 s down, push back in about 1 s
prescription.progression: Walking overhead lunges, then a light plate or dumbbell held overhead.

cues.text: Stand tall and reach both arms straight overhead, palms facing, biceps by the ears; ribs down.
Take a long step forward and land heel first; the arms stay stacked over the shoulders.
Breathe in and lower the back knee toward the floor; trunk tall, arms vertical.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to step back to standing.
Stand tall, arms still up; switch legs on the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Keep the arms beside the ears and the hands over the shoulders; look straight ahead.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to keep the arms up
mistakes.fix: Brace the ribs down; lower the arms a little if the back arches.
Keep the front knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.
Step long enough that the front shin is close to vertical at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); a step about one leg length was suggested as optimal for strength training (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Lowers to just above the floor, about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upright: the raised arms need a vertical trunk (clinical opinion); more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)
Vertical over the shoulders, elbows straight (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #21174, Bodyweight Overhead Forward Lunge (male), video (movement reference)
Hip, knee and ankle joint moments in the single-legged squat, forward lunge and reverse lunge (J Athl Train; PMC4641539)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)
Aspe & Swinton 2014, electromyographic and kinetic comparison of the back squat and overhead squat (J Strength Cond Res 28(10):2827-2836)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Skip the overhead reach if lifting the arms is painful; hands on the hips work the legs the same way.
Balance concerns: practise next to a wall or support.
modify: Shoulder limits: hands on the hips or arms crossed on the chest.
Knee discomfort: shorter range, back knee higher.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down under the raised arms; an overhead position raised anterior trunk activity only slightly in squats (Aspe 2014).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the arm up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the arm up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Lift and rotate the shoulder blade for the overhead reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Lift and rotate the shoulder blade for the overhead reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade upward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blade upward (clinical opinion).
